facts.raw_span: a 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
noted by his wife to have recently grown and acquired a crust
a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule was discovered on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement
the tumor had acquired a flakier surface
The specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
Negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains
Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei

Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present

concepts.why: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures, supports the diagnosis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
The well-circumscribed papule with a flakier surface and the presence of pseudohorn cysts are characteristic of Keratoacanthoma.

The proliferation of neoplastic cells and the involvement of many hairs are features that can be seen in Basal Cell Carcinoma, although the presence of malignant squamous cells suggests a different primary diagnosis.

The clear cell change and the negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor could suggest Sebaceous Carcinoma, but the overall clinical and histological picture is more consistent with Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
The presence of a well-circumscribed papule and pseudohorn cysts could suggest Actinic Keratosis, but the malignant features and the involvement of the dermis are not typical of this condition.

The presence of malignant squamous cells and the involvement of the epidermis are features of Intraepidermal Carcinoma, but the clinical and histological picture is more consistent with a more invasive carcinoma.

The clear cell change and the negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor could suggest Adenocarcinoma, but the overall clinical and histological picture is more consistent with Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The presence of malignant cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and the involvement of the dermis are features of Merkel Cell Carcinoma, but the clinical and histological picture is more consistent with Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
